rules.pattern: In this study, male Wistar rats weighing 190-210 grams were randomly divided into 8 groups
rules.replacement: We randomised 8 groups of male Wistar rats (190-210 g) after acclimation

rules.pattern: Group 2 \(diabetic control\) received physiological serum for 2 weeks and then were induced with diabetes using streptozotocin, followed by an additional 6 weeks of physiological serum
rules.replacement: Group 2 (diabetic control) had a 2-week physiological serum period, streptozotocin diabetes induction, then 6 weeks of vehicle

rules.pattern: Groups 3 to 6 received physiological serum for 2 weeks, were induced with diabetes, and then treated with nettle extract, fenugreek extract, and a combination of both extracts, respectively, for 6 weeks
rules.replacement: For groups 3-6, we used a 2-week run-in, STZ to induce diabetes, then 6 weeks of nettle extract, fenugreek extract, or both extracts, respectively

rules.pattern: Group 7 received physiological serum for 2 weeks, were induced with diabetes, and then treated with glibenclamide for 6 weeks
rules.replacement: Group 7 followed the same 2-week run-in and STZ diabetes protocol, then received glibenclamide for 6 weeks

rules.pattern: Measurements of blood glucose, insulin levels, and body weight were performed at various stages: before diabetes induction, 2-3 days after diabetes induction, 2 weeks after the start of treatment, and 6 weeks after diabetes induction
rules.replacement: Glucose, insulin, and body weight were checked at baseline, 2-3 days post-STZ, at 2 weeks on treatment, and at week 6 after diabetes induction

rules.pattern: The results indicated that nettle and fenugreek extracts, both individually and in combination, were effective in reducing blood glucose levels, increasing insulin levels, and decreasing body weight in diabetic rats
rules.replacement: With nettle, fenugreek, or both, diabetic rats had lower glucose and body weight and higher insulin

rules.pattern: Additionally, the efficacy of these extracts was comparable to the commonly used diabetes drug, glibenclamide
rules.replacement: Effects matched those seen with the diabetes drug glibenclamide

rules.pattern: This study suggests that nettle and fenugreek extracts could be considered as complementary herbal medicines in the treatment of diabetes
rules.replacement: Nettle and fenugreek extracts may work as add-on herbal options in diabetes care

rules.pattern: The results indicate that these extracts can effectively reduce blood glucose levels and increase insulin levels while also reducing body weight
rules.replacement: In treated rats, glucose fell, insulin rose, and body weight declined

rules.pattern: However, to confirm these findings and determine the appropriate dosage, clinical studies on humans are necessary
rules.replacement: Clinical work in patients is required to verify dose and benefit

rules.pattern: Such studies could help scientists and physicians develop the best therapeutic strategies for diabetes management and improve the quality of life for diabetic patients
rules.replacement: Such work could help clinicians improve diabetes care and patient quality of life
